summary.text: Hawking radiation is thermal radiation released outside a black hole's event horizon through quantum effects, in a model developed by Stephen Hawking in 1974.
It carries away mass and energy, so black holes that gain nothing else are expected to shrink and vanish, very slowly for all but the smallest.
Its temperature is inversely proportional to mass, so tiny black holes would radiate more and end in a burst of high-energy radiation that has not yet been detected.

facts.label: Detectability
facts.value: Far below what current telescopes can detect

facts.label: Temperature rule
facts.value: Inversely proportional to the black hole's mass

items.prompt: Older models said nothing inside an event horizon could escape. What did Hawking's work add?

options.label: Light inside can leave through the poles
Quantum effects make a black hole emit thermal radiation
Black holes stop pulling on outside matter
Event horizons can be crossed outward

items.explain: Applying quantum field theory, Hawking found a black hole continuously emits thermal blackbody radiation.

items.prompt: Compare a tiny primordial black hole with a giant one. Which radiates more strongly for its mass?

options.label: The giant one, since it holds more energy
They radiate identically
The tiny one, since temperature falls as mass rises
The one that is spinning faster only

items.explain: Hawking temperature is inversely proportional to mass, so small black holes radiate more and dissipate faster per mass.

items.prompt: Suppose a black hole stopped taking in any matter. What is its long-term fate?

options.label: It shrinks and eventually vanishes
It stays at the same size forever
It grows through radiation alone
It splits in two

items.explain: Hawking radiation reduces mass, so black holes that gain nothing are expected to shrink and ultimately vanish.

items.prompt: Jacob Bekenstein argued black holes have an entropy tied to which feature, implying they also have a temperature?

options.label: Their total spin
Their age
Their distance from Earth
Their surface area

items.explain: Bekenstein proposed finite entropy proportional to surface area, so black holes should also have a temperature.

items.prompt: In the vacuum-fluctuation picture, what results from a fluctuation right at the horizon?

options.label: A pair of particles that both fall in
A photon outside the horizon paired with one inside
A single particle flung outward
A burst that erases the horizon

items.explain: A fluctuation can produce a photon outside the horizon paired with one on the inside.

items.prompt: Why has no one observed Hawking radiation from a real black hole yet?

options.label: Black holes do not emit it at all
It only appears at the singularity
It is far too faint for telescopes to detect
It is blocked by the accretion disk

items.explain: The radiation is predicted to be many orders of magnitude below the best telescopes' detecting ability.
